ModelCharacter: The original Greenline breakthrough model: a J&J-designed Slovenian sedan cruiser that combined a very efficient low-drag hull, single shaft drive, roof-integrated solar and optional hybrid propulsion in a genuinely trailer-adjacent 33-foot package.
DesignLineage: The Greenline 33 launched the Greenline hybrid-cruiser concept around 2010.
Diesel-only, diesel-electric hybrid and later full-electric versions are propulsion variants of the same hull/model.
The model's long production run allowed major evolution in battery chemistry, solar output and hybrid controls without changing the canonical identity.

OwnershipCharacter: Exceptionally low hotel-energy demand and single-shaft simplicity in diesel form; hybrid/electric boats add battery, inverter and control-system complexity. Aging early-generation lithium/hybrid hardware should be evaluated as carefully as the diesel machinery.

ModelCharacter: A radically beamy 37-foot full-displacement liveaboard whose raised pilothouse, 15'10" beam and home-scale appliances deliver interior volume comparable to much longer trawlers. Twin tiny diesels, 2'10" draft and huge tankage make it a purpose-built coastal/Loop liveaboard rather than a conventional narrow trawler.
DesignLineage: Mirage Manufacturing launched the first GH37 in March 1997 after Ken Fickett and naval architect Lou Codega developed the design.
The GH37 was the original Great Harbour trawler and led to the GH47, N37 and N47.
The GH37 uses a raised pilothouse to maximize multi-level interior volume.
Production is now suspended; factory material remains available to support the brokerage/owner fleet.
OwnershipCharacter: Exceptionally low propulsion load—twin 54 hp diesels—but enormous beam, 48,000-pound loaded displacement and household-scale systems create big-boat logistics. Shallow draft, twin protected shafts and a stand-up machinery space are major service advantages.

ModelVariations.Name: Power versus motorsailer configuration
ModelVariations.Description: The Nomad is a pocket-trawler powerboat; the Kodiak is a pilothouse sailboat/motorsailer; the Wanderer was offered with or without a sailing rig. These are materially different use cases despite shared Nimble/Ted Brewer design language.

ModelCharacter: A genuinely tiny Ted Brewer-designed pocket trawler built around simplicity, highway trailering and protected-water cruising. The Nomad uses a single outboard in a well, an 8'6" beam, shallow draft and a compact pilothouse/cabin arrangement to provide surprising cruising utility at roughly seven knots.
DesignLineage: The Nimble Nomad was designed by Ted Brewer and entered production around 1990.
Owner records identify approximately 130 boats built, making the Nomad the most numerous of Nimble's power-cruiser designs.
The outboard-in-well arrangement and shallow, easily trailered hull distinguish it from Nimble's later diesel-powered Wanderer.
Ted Brewer himself owned a Nomad for years, reinforcing that the design was intended as a practical small cruising boat rather than a novelty.
OwnershipCharacter: Among the simplest cruising boats in B-Atlas: one small outboard, modest electrical and plumbing systems, shallow draft and true trailerability. The principal risks are age, trailer condition, water intrusion, old wiring and owner modifications rather than propulsion complexity.

ModelCharacter: A heavily built Taiwanese full-displacement tri-cabin trawler with two private sleeping cabins, two heads, extensive teak and the classic single Ford Lehman 120 installation that defined economical 1970s cruising.
DesignLineage: Verified 1977–1981 boats were built by Universal Marine Co. Ltd. in Taipei, Taiwan.
The design appears under both Universal Marine and distributor/secondary names such as Litton, reflecting common private-label practice among Taiwanese builders of the era.
Universal Marine later became associated with construction of early Ocean Alexander yachts, but the Universal 36 remains a distinct builder/model identity.
Single- and twin-engine examples exist; B-Atlas represents the common single-Lehman tri-cabin configuration while leaving listing-specific machinery authoritative.
OwnershipCharacter: Very economical and simple in single-Lehman form, with a spacious teak interior and strong full-displacement cruising character. Original teak decks, deckhouse leaks, black-iron tanks, old wiring and extensive woodwork are the primary age-related ownership exposures.
